insights.insight: The 7-day window crossed 2,000 confirmed receipts for the first time on record, peaking at $87,942.39 GMV before rolloff — the second-highest 7-day GMV figure ever observed. This is deterministic purchase proof, not modeled intent.

insights.topic: Grocery dominance with high-value unknown segment
insights.insight: Grocery-supermarkets anchor the receipt pool at 28.3% of 14-day receipts, but the unattributed 'Unknown' category carries an $85.59 average ticket versus $45.07 for grocery — nearly double — signaling a high-value spend segment that remains unclassified and potentially underbid by category-targeted campaigns.

insights.topic: Retailer concentration at mass and warehouse channels
insights.insight: Walmart (332 receipts), Kroger (154), and Costco (128) account for the three largest verified brand footprints in the 14-day window, confirming the receipt pool skews toward high-frequency, high-basket mass retail — the exact channel where cookieless targeting alternatives are most commercially relevant.

insights.topic: Settlement freeze against active receipt intake
insights.insight: Payout count (809) and total sats claimed (15,415,419) have been frozen across every observed heartbeat while receipt accumulation continues uninterrupted past 107,500 cumulative receipts — the divergence between active data intake and frozen settlement is the primary structural risk signal for any brand considering this as a live data supply.

The 14-day window has crossed $200,000 on four distinct reads, with the all-time high reaching $211,448.13 on 2026-11-26T20:15 — but UTC midnight rolloffs consistently pull the window below that threshold before recovery, meaning $200K is a recurring cycle ceiling, not a stable floor.

Store entropy has reached 3.033 bits across 10 DKIM vendors spanning grocery, dining, department stores, gas, and convenience — the receipt pool is broadening across spend categories, which expands the addressable audience segments available for cookieless targeting use cases.
